verdict.rationale: Lium documents fully browser-free operation: an agent can sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods with no browser. Its CLI is built for scripts, with `lium exec` returning the remote command's exit code, `--ttl` auto-removal, scoped API keys with server-enforced budgets, and stable `error.code` values to branch on. This is the core of headless automation; the probe's 404 on docs.lium.io OpenAPI paths does not contradict the documented lium.io/api/openapi.json location. missing for 10: an explicit CI-pipeline guide (e.g., CI-runner examples or env-var non-interactive auth docs), independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
lium exec job "nvidia-smi"                              # exits with the remote command's exit code
An AI agent with only a shell can rent, use and release a GPU on its own.
**`error.code`** is stable. Branch on it, not on the message.
